concepts.label: Couchbase Transactions (Couchbase Server)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the general server-side local-transaction feature this page describes and links to (server/current/learn/data/transactions.md); distinct from the n1ql: family (n1ql:begin-transaction, n1ql:active-transaction-record etc.), which models the SQL++ statement surface for distributed transactions specifically, whereas this page's own framing is 'local transactions... either to the Couchbase Server or to the Couchbase Lite database' - a broader, less statement-specific notion. Kept apart per the no-silent-merge rule

relations.subject: sgw:sync-gateway-instance
relations.evidence: Changes made on the server within a transaction block are guaranteed to be imported by the Sync Gateway only after all the changes in a transaction are committed.

relations.subject: server:transactions
relations.evidence: There is no guarantee that a series of updates made within a transaction block, on either the Couchbase Server or Couchbase Lite client side, will be ACID compliant when they sync to the other end.

notable_absence.finding: The page states Couchbase Lite also 'supports transactions that are local to the Couchbase Lite database' via Database.inBatch(), a Couchbase-Lite-side concept entirely outside this extraction's scope (sync-gateway/ only) - no relation was extracted for the Couchbase Lite half of this page's comparison since it names no Sync-Gateway-side mechanism, only a cross-reference to CBL's own API docs.

cross_component_finding: This is the only page in the batch that explicitly denies an ACID guarantee across the Sync Gateway/Couchbase Lite/Couchbase Server boundary - every other compatibility page in this batch describes what IS supported or version-gated; this one's central point is a limit on what replication can promise at all, regardless of version.
